title: The Lean Startup: How Today's Entrepreneurs Use Continuous Innovation to Create Radically Successful Businesses
author: Eric Ries
primary_purpose: To change the way startups and established companies innovate, manage product development, and respond to market realities by offering a scientific, systematic framework focused on learning, rapid iteration, and efficiency.

structure_format.organization: Divided into three main parts: Vision (the Lean Startup principles), Steer (MVP, measurement, and learning), and Accelerate (techniques for rapid innovation and scaling). Each chapter blends theory with real-world examples.
features: Case studies from startups and established companies
Step-by-step explanations of Lean Startup methods
Frameworks and terminology unique to Lean Startup (e.g., Build-Measure-Learn loop)

key_concepts_lessons: Startups exist to learn how to build a sustainable business.
Progress is measured through validated learning, not just product shipment or revenue.
The Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop is at the heart of successful startups.
Launching early with a minimum viable product is crucial to gathering real customer insights.
Continuous innovation and iterative experimentation help startups discover what works.
Pivoting (changing direction) is sometimes necessary to find product/market fit.
Lean Startup principles can be applied at any stage and in all types of organizations, not just technology startups.
notable_features: Origin of widely used startup vocabulary (e.g., MVP, pivot, innovation accounting)
Framework for reducing product development risk
Actionable strategies for startups and established companies
Widely adopted by accelerators, entrepreneurship programs, and innovation labs
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2011 during a boom in startup activity and heightened interest in tech entrepreneurship, the book responded to widespread frustrations with high startup failure rates and inefficient product launches. It synthesized principles from lean manufacturing, agile development, and entrepreneurship into a single methodology.
reception_impact: Became a bestselling business book and foundational text in startup ecosystems worldwide
Led to widespread adoption of Lean Startup methods in startups, corporates, and government
Cited as a major influence on 21st-century entrepreneurship and innovation practices
Criticized by some for being overly focused on tech startups or for oversimplifying traditional business fundamentals
comparable_titles: The Startup Owner’s Manual by Steve Blank & Bob Dorf
Zero to One by Peter Thiel
